Consult Summary:
- Video consult for an adult female runner with a 2-week history of right knee pain and clicking provoked by running and certain gym movements; advised rest/ice, prescribed a stronger NSAID (details not documented), physiotherapy referral, red flag precautions, and possible imaging if indicated.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Right knee pain and clicking after increasing running for marathon training.
  - Occasional post-run tingling in right toes (single episode; resolved).
- Timeline:
  - Began ~2 weeks ago after starting longer runs ~1 month ago.
  - Pain now occurs ~20 minutes into runs (approx. mile 2.5–3) and has worsened to the point of stopping runs.
  - Initial mild swelling after the first long run resolved with ice; no current swelling.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Worse with running >20 minutes and ab exercises involving knee flexion/extension transitions.
  - Improved with rest and ice.
  - Ibuprofen used as needed.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Clicking during certain gym movements.
  - Single episode of tingling in right toes post-run; resolved; no persistent numbness.
  - Reports sock indentations after prolonged standing; denies calf pain.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No knee giving way/instability, no locking, no issues with stairs or normal walking.
  - Full ability to fully flex and extend the knee.
  - No current swelling, redness, warmth, or pain at rest.
  - No color or temperature changes in lower legs/feet.
  - No foot arch pain or joint pain in the feet.
- Systems review:
  - Denies asthma, GI problems (indigestion, reflux).

Past Medical History:
- Refractive error (farsighted); s/p LASIK.
- Severe UTI in the past; kidney stones considered; ER visit (details/outcome not specified).
- Sports injury a few months ago (ice hockey fall → large bruise); no ongoing issues reported.

Social History:
- Highly active: training for a marathon (runs typically 4–8 miles), gym several times per week, plays ice hockey.
- Substance use: occasional cannabis (smokes a joint).
- Tobacco and alcohol use not discussed.
- Lives in London (address provided in consult); occupational/living situation not discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed; route/frequency beyond “as needed” not documented.
- Aleve (naproxen) as needed; dose/route/frequency not documented (patient unsure of class).
- Vitamin D; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Melatonin; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescription: stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed; name/dose/route/frequency not documented; instructed not to use concurrently with ibuprofen and to take with food.

Allergies:
- Not discussed; not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not recorded.
- Musculoskeletal (per patient report during video consult):
  - Right knee: currently not swollen; full active range of motion (can fully flex and extend).
  - No locking; no giving way/instability.
  - Able to walk and use stairs without issues.
  - No calf tenderness reported.
- Neurovascular (per history):
  - No current numbness/tingling; no color/temperature changes.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Imaging to be considered after physiotherapy assessment if indicated for cartilage/ligament pathology.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms in a runner; onset ~2 weeks; provoked by running and certain gym movements; initial transient swelling; no locking/instability; full ROM.
  - Plan:
    - Reduce/ease up on running; avoid running through pain.
    - Continue regular ice therapy.
    - Start stronger NSAID as prescribed; take with food; do not combine with ibuprofen (medication details not documented).
    - Refer to physiotherapy for comprehensive assessment and initial management.
    - Consider imaging (e.g., to evaluate cartilage/ligaments) based on physiotherapy findings.
    - Safety-net: seek urgent care for persistent/worsening swelling, heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks or cannot bend/straighten.
    - Follow-up: attend physiotherapy; if wait is prolonged, option to be seen in clinic for examination.
- Issue 2: Transient right toe tingling post-run; resolved; no ongoing neurovascular symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor; no immediate workup given resolution.
    - Return if recurrence, persistence, or if accompanied by weakness, numbness, color/temperature changes, or calf pain.

General plan items:
- Medication reconciliation and allergy status to be confirmed at next in-person visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: allergy history; detailed medication doses/routes/frequencies; vitals; clinician-performed knee exam; tobacco/alcohol use; full past surgical history; family history.
- Internal conflicts: early reference to “both knees” vs later clarification of pain localized to right knee—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Good; clear overall with conversational fillers; no major inaudible sections.
